stem: Hydraulic brakes and hydraulic lifts (used to raise heavy vehicles in a garage) work on the principle that pressure applied at any point in an enclosed, incompressible liquid is transmitted equally and undiminished in all directions. This principle is known as:
explanation: Pascal's Law explains how a small force on a narrow piston can produce a much larger force on a wider piston in a hydraulic system, since pressure is transmitted equally throughout the enclosed liquid — distinct from Archimedes' Principle, which concerns the upward buoyant force on an object submerged in a fluid.
